extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly / scientifically curious general public (late 19th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Short popular-science news and explanatory pieces reporting recent observations, experiments, and practical recommendations across natural history, technology, and medicine for a general educated audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalogue inclusion and arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The catalogue is intended to embrace independent journals of pure and applied science, published in all countries, from 1665 to 1880; the arrangement of titles will be strictly alphabetical, grouping periodicals having different names at different periods under the heading of the first or earliest title of the series, with cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give minute details concerning changes of title, sequence of series, editorship, and date of publication; present synoptical tables containing the dates of publication of each volume (using a method slightly modified from Professor James D. Dana); include a limited number of periodicals in the synoptical tables, preferring those published during a long series of years or issued very irregularly; do not embrace transactions of learned societies (these belong in Scudder's Catalogue of Scientific Serials); include every branch of applied science and represent many languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of meteor radiant centers
rubrics_metrics.description: To give a character of certainty to the existence of centers (radiant points of meteor currents), the determination should rest upon the definition of an adequate number of trajectories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification requires continued observations and an adequate number of trajectories to define distinct centers; counting large samples of meteors and estimating observational incompleteness (e.g., estimating percent escaped) strengthens inference; distribution of hourly means and intersection of paths (as observed near Fomalhaut) can indicate direction of motion relative to the earth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors influencing rainfall (principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rain chiefly occurs when the wind from the ocean is blowing toward the mountains; extraordinary rainfalls at many stations are probably due to the influence of nearby elevated mountains which deflect wind upward causing vapor condensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider multiple influences modifying rainfall: elevation and proximity to mountains, presence of upward currents, descent of air after mountain crossing causing rain shadows, meeting of trade-winds producing rain belts, irregular barometric depressions indicating storms, proximity to the ocean when prevailing winds come from the sea, and projection of capes/headlands; uniformity of wind direction, obstruction by mountains, remoteness from ocean in prevailing-wind direction, and high latitude tend to produce dry climates; recognize exceptions and that more systematic and careful observations are required to determine real influence in some regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causation and control principles for salmon Saprolegnia disease
rubrics_metrics.description: The malady is assigned to diseases caused by parasitic organisms — the work of a minute fungus (Saprolegnia); Saprolegnia are essentially saprophytes ordinarily deriving nourishment from dead matter and only occasionally parasitic on living organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: zoospores diffused through water germinate and produce mycelium on healthy salmon skin; inoculation experiments (e.g., on dead house-flies) show the fungus's pathogenic potential; Saprolegnia causing salmon disease may exist in fresh waters where dead insects infested by Saprolegnia are met; they do not appear on decaying bodies in salt water. Policy implication: 'the careful extirpation of every diseased individual is the treatment theoretically indicated,' though in practice it may not always be worth while. Also note that pollution, drought, or over-stocking will not produce the disease if Saprolegnia are absent, although they may favor its spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photophone/‘teleradiophone’ multiplex signalling principle
rubrics_metrics.description: When the ray of light to a selenium receiver is eclipsed many times per second a continuous hum is produced; varying intermissions can produce signals analogous to Morse code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To send multiple messages on the same wire, multiply transmitters at one end and telephones at the other, rotate eclipsing wheels at different speeds to produce notes of different pitch, and fit resonators to enhance particular notes so each telephone responds primarily to a single note; complex currents flow through all telephones but each clerk hears only the particular note to which his instrument is tuned, allowing simultaneous and bidirectional messaging without confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe use of pneumatic perforators and pioneer-needle in gas-infected mines
rubrics_metrics.description: Perforators worked by compressed air can make drill holes to receive powder, dispensing with hand-drilling; in gas-infected coal-mines, powder cannot be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a needle-wedge (pioneer-drill / 'bosseyeuse') substituted for powder: insert two segmental iron bars to fill the drill-hole, introduce a conical steel needle into the cylinder and drive it like a wedge by the perforator piston to force the segments apart and split the rock; introduce powder only when the perforator hole reaches about twenty-seven inches if powder is to be used; multiple drilled holes as required depending on rock hardness; this method enables mechanical rock-breaking and reduces explosions in gas-infected mines while approaching nearly the speed of gunpowder in average veins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental method for measuring ground vibrations from surface traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure transmission of vibrations from railroad trains through the ground by fixing cups containing mercury at stations at known distances and noting disturbance via displacements of the reflected image of the pole-star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place sensors at various distances (example distances: 0.29 to 0.93 miles) and observe how effects vary with distance from train, nature of the ground, and type of train; expect potential interruptions of shallow-depth vibrations by features like ravines; test other sources (e.g., carriage driving) to determine thresholds (distance at which temporary shaking is observed) and characterize dependence on local conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative anatomical and developmental criteria for brachiopod classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Brachiopods must be distinguished from mollusks as they represent a different type of development; detailed comparative anatomy shows agreement of brachiopods with annelids rather than with mollusks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve systematic position by minute comparative analyses of anatomy and development (embryology), following the approach of Steenstrup and Morse; use detailed similarity/difference in developmental type and anatomical structures to infer phylogenetic affinities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes and regimen-based treatment recommendations for obesity
rubrics_metrics.description: Obesity's principal danger is lesions of the heart; causes include excess of food and alcoholic drinks, too much sleep, and occasionally marriage; treatment requires sustained physical activity and dietary regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of rapid severe dieting that can cause loss of strength and regain of weight; recommended regimen example: daily active early-morning exercise (horseback-riding, gymnastics, fencing), severe dietary restrictions such as skipping breakfast after fatiguing exercise or taking a minimal breakfast (eggs, cutlet with salad and fruit), coffee without sugar, no bread or wine, water or unsweetened tea for drink; dinner with no soup, plate of meat, green vegetables, fruit, no bread or wine; avoid dining in the city and practice absolute self-restraint. Note demographic observations (e.g., higher liability in women with alcoholism, prostitution, or inactivity) and that obesity may occur at any age.
